meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Thu 29 Oct: NIFTY 50 dips as IT weighs; Brent near $115

brief: Benchmarks closed lower on Wednesday: the NIFTY 50 fell 0.22% to 22,698.85 and the Sensex 0.48%, as IT and oil and gas shares weighed, while midcap and smallcap indices edged up.
Foreign and domestic institutions were both net buyers (provisional), while the rupee weakened 21 paise to a provisional 95.28 per dollar, with Brent crude near $115 a barrel.
Overnight, the US Federal Reserve kept its policy range at 3.75% to 4.00%. Today brings results from Coal India, Asian Paints and IndiGo, and the European Central Bank's decision this evening.

stories.headline: The US Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75% to 4.00%, with two members voting for a hike
stories.what: The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10 to 2 on 28 October to keep its policy range unchanged after September's quarter-point increase. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack preferred an immediate 25 basis point hike. Reuters reported that CME FedWatch odds of a December hike rose to about 85% from 78% a day earlier.
stories.why: US interest rates influence the dollar and the relative appeal of emerging-market assets. That feeds into the rupee and into foreign portfolio flows into Indian shares and bonds.

stories.headline: Brent crude settled above $115 a barrel; reports pointed to Middle East supply risks
stories.what: Brent settled 1.3% higher at $115.32 on 28 October, after a Wall Street Journal report that the US had told Gulf states to prepare for a possible short campaign against Iran. Recent Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and a fourth straight weekly fall in US crude stocks were also cited.
stories.why: India imports most of the crude oil it uses, so higher prices raise the import bill and the demand for dollars. That is a channel to fuel costs, inflation and the rupee.

stories.headline: The rupee weakened 21 paise to 95.28 per US dollar
stories.what: The rupee closed at a provisional 95.28 per dollar on 28 October, from 95.07 on Tuesday, after opening at 95.01 and touching 95.29. Dealers pointed to a firmer dollar, higher crude prices and elevated US Treasury yields.
stories.why: A weaker rupee raises the rupee cost of imports such as crude oil. Currency moves also change the rupee value of overseas assets, including those held by international funds, in either direction.

stories.headline: Industrial output grew 6.7% in September, slower than August's revised 7.8%
stories.what: Quick estimates released on 28 October put September growth in the Index of Industrial Production at 6.7% year on year. Manufacturing rose 7.6% and electricity 11.2%, while mining contracted 6.2%; capital goods grew 10.4% and consumer non-durables 1.4%.
stories.why: The IIP tracks factory, mining and power output each month. It feeds into GDP estimates and gives an early read on the industrial activity behind many listed companies' sales.

stories.headline: Hindustan Unilever's quarterly sales grew 14.8% while its margin narrowed
stories.what: For July to September 2026, Hindustan Unilever reported turnover of ₹18,071 crore, up 14.8%, with underlying volume growth of 7%. Profit attributable to owners rose 3.9% to ₹2,790 crore, helped by a year-ago loss from discontinued operations; reported profit after tax of ₹2,796 crore was flat. The EBITDA margin fell 140 basis points to 22.6%, and the board declared an interim dividend of ₹19 per share.
stories.why: HUL's volume growth is widely read as a gauge of household consumption, which matters for the consumer companies held across many diversified equity funds.

stories.headline: Hero MotoCorp's quarterly profit rose 41%, helped by a one-time gain
stories.what: Hero MotoCorp's consolidated net profit for July to September 2026 rose 41% to ₹1,860.55 crore, including a one-time gain of ₹397 crore, and revenue from operations rose 23% to ₹14,970.50 crore. Vehicle sales rose 10% to 18.68 lakh units, with scooters up 47%.
stories.why: Two-wheeler sales are a widely tracked indicator of mass-market consumer demand.

global.headline: Wall Street closed slightly higher after the Fed held rates; GIFT Nifty traded lower by morning
global.note: In Asian trade on Thursday, Nasdaq futures were about 1% lower after Alphabet shares fell around 10% after hours on its results, and the US 10-year Treasury yield was 4.98%. US yields and the dollar shape foreign portfolio flows into India. GIFT Nifty is an early indication of how the NIFTY 50 may open, not a forecast.

mf.headline: SIP contributions reached ₹32,490 crore in September as equity funds drew ₹38,307 crore

stats.label: Industry assets

highlights.text: Small-cap, mid-cap and flexi-cap funds drew the most equity money, at ₹9,039 crore, ₹7,835 crore and ₹6,702 crore, together about three-fifths of the month's equity inflow.

Debt funds saw net redemptions of about ₹1.83 lakh crore, led by liquid and money market funds. AMFI's note attributes them mainly to tax-related liquidity needs ahead of advance tax deadlines, as the 10-year G-Sec yield rose to 7.18% by 30 September.
Gold ETFs took in ₹4,451 crore, about 71% more than in August. That was before mid-October, when fund houses paused fresh money into gold ETF fund of funds (see rule changes below).

regulatory.text: The Monetary Policy Committee raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, its first increase since February 2023, and moved its stance to calibrated tightening. Bond prices move opposite to yields, and funds holding longer-dated bonds see larger price changes in either direction.

Stopped accepting fresh lump sums, switch-ins and new SIP or STP registrations in gold ETF fund of funds, reportedly at SEBI's instruction. Existing SIPs and STPs, redemptions and switch-outs continue, and no end date has been given.

Amendments to the Mutual Funds Regulations replace the mutual-fund-specific advertisement code with the common code for intermediaries, from the 180th day after the 9 October gazette notification (about 7 April 2027).

nfo_summary.text: Cafemutual's list showed twelve new fund offers open on 29 October: four sectoral or thematic index funds and ETFs, two silver products (an ETF and its fund of funds), two multi-asset funds of funds, two active equity funds (large and mid cap; small cap), an equity savings fund and a sectoral debt fund. Each scheme's risk level and terms are set out in its scheme information document.

learn.title: How your SIP shows up in the daily DII number
paragraphs: Every evening, the exchanges publish provisional figures for how much foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and domestic institutional investors (DIIs) bought and sold in the cash market. On 28 October, DIIs bought ₹643 crore more than they sold.

DIIs include mutual funds, insurance companies, banks and pension funds. When SIP instalments reach fund houses each month (₹32,490 crore in September, from about 10 crore contributing SIP accounts), the equity funds among them invest that money in shares, and the buying appears in the DII figure.

That is why market reports compare the two. FII flows can swing with global conditions, while regular SIP money gives domestic funds a steady stream to invest. Provisional figures for October up to the 28th show FIIs as net sellers of about ₹47,817 crore and DIIs as net buyers of about ₹61,113 crore.
